arxiv-1802-02613.title: Measurement of the inelastic proton-proton cross section at s = 13 ​ \TeV \sqrt{s}=13\TeV
arxiv-1802-02613.description: Abstract A measurement of the inelastic proton-proton cross section with the CMS detector at a center-of-mass energy of s = 13 ​ \TeV \sqrt{s}=13\TeV is presented. The analysis is based on events with energy deposits in the forward calorimeters, which cover pseudorapidities of − 6.6 < η < − 3.0 -6.6<\eta<-3.0 and + 3.0 < η < + 5.2 +3.0<\eta<+5.

arxiv-1809-03767.title: Observations of high and low Fe charge states in individual solar wind streams with coronal-hole origin
arxiv-1809-03767.creator: Verena Heidrich-Meisner, Thies Peleikis, Martin Kruse, Lars Berger, and Robert Wimmer-Schweingruber
arxiv-1809-03767.description: Abstract Context. The solar wind originating from coronal holes is comparatively well-understood and is characterized by lower densities and average charge states compared to the so-called slow solar wind. Except for wave perturbations, the average properties of the coronal-hole solar wind are passably constant. Aims.

arxiv-1809-04335.title: Graphyne as the anode material of magnesium-ion batteries: ab initio study
arxiv-1809-04335.creator: E. Shomali a, I. Abdolhosseini Sarsari* a,b, F. Tabatabaei a, MR. Mosaferi a, N. Seriani c
arxiv-1809-04335.description: Abstract Graphyne, a single atomic layer structure of the carbon six-member rings connected by one acetilenic linkage, is a promising anode of rechargeable batteries. In this paper, a first-principle study has been carried out on graphyne as a new candidate for the anode material of magnesium-ion batteries, using density functional theory calculations.

arxiv-2205-15217.title: GraphWalks: Efficient Shape Agnostic Geodesic Shortest Path Estimation
arxiv-2205-15217.creator: Rolandos Alexandros Potamias, Alexandros Neofytou, Kyriaki Margarita Bintsi, Stefanos Zafeiriou
arxiv-2205-15217.description: Abstract Geodesic paths and distances are among the most popular intrinsic properties of 3D surfaces. Traditionally, geodesic paths on discrete polygon surfaces were computed using shortest path algorithms, such as Dijkstra. However, such algorithms have two major limitations. They are non-differentiable which limits their direct usage in learnable pipelines and they are considerably time demanding.

arxiv-2208-10655.title: Symmetry Relation Database and Its Application to Ferroelectric Materials Discovery
arxiv-2208-10655.creator: Qiang Zhu, Byungkyun Kang, Kevin Parrish
arxiv-2208-10655.description: Abstract The ability to understand the atomistic mechanisms that occur in the solid phase transition is of crucial importance in materials research. To investigate the displacive phase transition at the atomic scale, we have implemented a numerical algorithm to automate the detection of the symmetry relations between any two candidate crystal structures.

arxiv-2307-02269.title: SpaceNLI: Evaluating the Consistency of Predicting Inferences In Space
arxiv-2307-02269.creator: Lasha Abzianidze Joost Zwarts Yoad Winter
arxiv-2307-02269.description: Abstract While many natural language inference (NLI) datasets target certain semantic phenomena, e.g., negation, tense & aspect, monotonicity, and presupposition, to the best of our knowledge, there is no NLI dataset that involves diverse types of spatial expressions and reasoning. We fill this gap by semi-automatically creating an NLI dataset for spatial reasoning, called SpaceNLI. 1 1 1 https://github.

arxiv-2411-12176.title: Hidden Markov model analysis to fluorescence blinking of fluorescently labeled DNA
arxiv-2411-12176.creator: Tatsuhiro Furuta, Shuya Fan, Tadao Takada, Yohei Kondo, Mamoru Fujitsuka, Atsushi Maruyama, Kiyohiko Kawai, Kazuma Nakamura
arxiv-2411-12176.description: Abstract We examine quantitatively the transition process from emitting to not-emitting states of fluorescent molecules with a machine learning technique. In a fluorescently labeled DNA, the fluorescence occurs continuously under irradiation, but it often transfers to the not-emitting state corresponding to a charge-separated state.

arxiv-2508-12416.title: fCrit : A Visual Explanation System for Furniture Design Creative Support Conference: Explainable AI for the Arts Workshop 2025; June 23, 2025; Online
arxiv-2508-12416.creator: Vuong Nguyen and Gabriel Vigliensoni
arxiv-2508-12416.description: A 2025 arXiv research paper by Vuong Nguyen and Gabriel Vigliensoni. We introduce fCrit , a dialogue-based AI system designed to critique furniture design with a focus on explainability. Grounded in reflective learning and formal analysis, fCrit employs a multi-agent architecture informed by a structured design knowledge base. We argue that explainability in the arts should not only make AI reasoning transparent but also adapt to the ways users think and talk about their designs.

arxiv-2512-24801.title: Limits of quantum generative models with classical sampling hardness
arxiv-2512-24801.creator: Sabrina Herbst, Ivona Brandić, Adrián Pérez-Salinas
arxiv-2512-24801.description: Abstract Sampling tasks have been successful in establishing quantum advantages both in theory and experiments. This has fueled the use of quantum computers for generative modeling to create samples following the probability distribution underlying a given dataset. In particular, the potential to build generative models on classically hard distributions would immediately preclude classical simulability, due to theoretical separations.

pmc-10591051.title: Cancer-associated fibroblasts undergoing neoadjuvant chemotherapy suppress rectal cancer revealed by single-cell and spatial transcriptomics
pmc-10591051.creator: Pengfei Qin, Huaxian Chen, Yuhang Wang, Liang Huang, Ke Huang, Guozhong Xiao, Changpeng Han, Jiancong Hu, Dezheng Lin, Xingyang Wan, Yihui Zheng, Yufeng Liu, Guiming Li, Haojie Yang, Shubiao Ye, Minyi Luo, Yuanji Fu, Hao Xu, Luping Wen, Zhiwei Guo, Xunan Shen, Zeyu Li, Chunqing Wang, Xi Chen, Linyin
pmc-10591051.description: SummaryNeoadjuvant chemotherapy (NAC) for rectal cancer (RC) shows promising clinical response. The modulation of the tumor microenvironment (TME) by NAC and its association with therapeutic response remain unclear. Here, we use single-cell RNA sequencing and spatial transcriptome sequencing to examine the cell dynamics in 29 patients with RC, who are sampled pairwise before and after treatment.

pmc-10738539.title: UNDERSTANDING THE IMPACT OF COVID-19 ON THE USE OF TRANSPORTATION SERVICES BY OREGON ASSISTED LIVING RESIDENTS
pmc-10738539.creator: Minju Kim, Ozcan Tunalilar, Paula Carder
pmc-10738539.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2023). COVID-19 has affected many aspects of daily life, including transportation. This study aims to understand the impact of the COVID-19 pandemic on the use of transportation services by residents of assisted living communities in Oregon. Primary data about transportation service availability and use were collected from 721 AL communities using mailed questionnaires, before (winter of 2020) and during the pandemic (winter of 2022).

pmc-11339649.title: Biomarkers of outcome in patients undergoing CD19 CAR‐T therapy for large B cell lymphoma
pmc-11339649.creator: Inna Y. Gong, Daisy Tran, Samuel Saibil, Rob C. Laister, John Kuruvilla
pmc-11339649.description: CD19‐directed autologous chimeric antigen receptor T cell (CAR‐T) therapy has transformed the management of relapsed/refractory (R/R) large B cell lymphoma (LBCL). Initially approved in the third line and beyond setting, CAR‐T is now standard of care (SOC) for second‐line treatment in patients with refractory disease or early relapse (progression within 12 months) following primary chemoimmunotherapy.

pmc-12643482.title: Comparative analysis of adenovirus, mRNA, and protein vaccines reveals context-dependent immunogenicity and efficacy
pmc-12643482.creator: Bakare Awakoaiye, Shiyi Li, Sarah Sanchez, Tanushree Dangi, Nahid Irani, Laura Arroyo, Gabriel Arellano, Shadi Mohammadabadi, Malika Aid, Pablo Penaloza-MacMaster
pmc-12643482.description: Despite the widespread use of adenovirus, mRNA, and protein-based vaccines during the COVID-19 pandemic, their relative immunological profiles and protective efficacies remain incompletely defined. Here, we compared antigen kinetics, innate and adaptive immune responses, and protective efficacy following Ad5, mRNA, and protein vaccination in mice.

pmc-12730708.title: Dasatinib Inhibits Basal B Breast Cancer Through ETS1-Mediated Extracellular Matrix Remodeling
pmc-12730708.creator: Xinyu Guo, Heng Sun, Feng Yu, Yangyang Feng, Sen Guo, Josh Haipeng Lei, Kai Miao, Ka-U Ip, Ling Li, Hanghang Li, Xiaohong Liao, Xiaoling Xu, Rong Zhou, Chu-Xia Deng
pmc-12730708.description: Background/Objectives: Developing effective therapies for patients with triple-negative breast cancer (TNBC) remains an urgent clinical priority. Compared with other subtypes, the basal B type of TNBC exhibits a less differentiated and mesenchymal-like phenotype that models highly invasive and metastatic breast malignancies. To target metastatic TNBC, our current study sought to identify effective therapeutic drugs and the underlying mechanisms.

pmc-12749735.title: Optimised comorbidity indices can reflect patient performance status in register based studies of prostate cancer
pmc-12749735.creator: Marcus Westerberg, Hans Garmo, Jesper Bonnedahl, Marie Hjälm Eriksson, David Robinson, Pär Stattin, Rolf Gedeborg
pmc-12749735.description: Eastern Cooperative Oncology Group Performance Status (ECOG-PS) is commonly used in cancer trials to select a study population with good performance, but ECOG-PS is rarely available in health-care registers. We assessed if patient age and comorbidity indices can substitute ECOG-PS when selecting men in register-based studies of advanced prostate cancer.
